solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Style of construction of a brick house (6)

indicators.note: to house is to hold inside, so the answer sits within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across these three words, starting after the O and stopping before the final K

explanation.surface: An architect describing how a brick house is built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' looks like part of the building talk but is the verb: the words 'of a brick' house the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabric of a building is its structure and the way it is made.

clue.text: Talent to burn brightly for the audience (5)

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the sound is what counts

blocks.note: to flare is to burn brightly

explanation.surface: A performer's talent blazing out in front of an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: FLARE and FLAIR are said the same way, so the verb is heard and the noun is written.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a flair for music is a natural gift for it.

clue.text: Hobart’s one server of drinks (9)

blocks.note: the surface suggests someone from the Tasmanian capital; the setter means the name itself, which keeps a drinking place in its middle
the straight reading, a person behind a pub counter

explanation.surface: A remark that the Tasmanian capital is a bartender.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the city name as letters: HOBART holds BAR in the middle, so it is literally a bar keeper, and 'server of drinks' confirms the everyday sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A barkeeper runs a bar and serves drinks.

clue.text: This writer’s embracing maiden — one making Friday call? (4)

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold something in your arms, so the first piece wraps the second

blocks.note: this writer's = the setter is = I AM
M = maiden (an over with no runs, in cricket scoring)

explanation.surface: A writer taking a girl in their arms, then asking who makes a call on Friday.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is 'is', not possession: this writer's = I AM, which then holds M after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads the Muslim congregation at Friday prayers.

clue.text: Something easy to do with a tree (8)

blocks.note: to do with = about = ON, as in 'a talk on birds'

explanation.surface: Someone asking what simple job could be done with a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reuses the 'a' that ends the wordplay: 'to do with' = ON, then A, and 'a tree' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The cinchona is the South American tree whose bark gives quinine.

clue.text: Pitch trendy Conservative policy (7)

blocks.note: the party line is its policy

explanation.surface: A political pitch for a fashionable Tory policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' sits at the front looking like a sales verb; it is the noun for a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: An incline is a slope, and a pitch is the slope of a roof or hill.

clue.text: Revolutionary wife, ace in crime, creating gossip (4,3,3)

indicators.note: the ace goes in the crime word

blocks.note: A = ace, as on playing cards

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's wife and her partner in crime giving the neighbours something to talk about.
explanation.walkthrough: Che Guevara is the crossword's standard revolutionary, and the commas make 'ace in crime' look like a master criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to chew the fat is to chat at length about nothing much, which is gossip.

clue.text: Playwright with men leading the fashion (5)

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so the men come before the fashion in the answer

blocks.note: OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
ton = the fashion, the fashionable set

explanation.surface: A dramatist whose men set the fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Orton was an English playwright of the 1960s (Loot, Entertaining Mr Sloane). TON for fashion is an old word crosswords keep alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Orton wrote black comedies for the London stage.

clue.text: Most severe wind is across the Channel (9)

blocks.note: Auster is the south wind, named for the Roman god
French for 'is'; France lies across the English Channel

explanation.surface: A weather report: the harshest gale is blowing over the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Across the Channel' means French, so 'is' becomes EST rather than a direction for the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severe, and austerest is its superlative.

clue.text: Worship always in part of school curriculum? (6)

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

blocks.note: RE = religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: Asking whether daily worship belongs on the school timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: Religious education is a compulsory subject in British schools; the question mark admits it is only one example of a curriculum part.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to revere a saint is to venerate, even worship, them.

clue.text: Area with an enclosure invaded by soldiers (7)

indicators.note: invaders get inside, so the soldiers go into the enclosure

explanation.surface: A plot of land with a fenced pen that troops have overrun.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are the crossword's usual squad of soldiers, and 'an' shrinks to its short form.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is an area of land measured in acres.

clue.text: Makes boxes to accommodate drug (7)

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so the boxes hold the drug

explanation.surface: A smuggler building boxes with room to hide narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes boxes' reads as one phrase about a carpenter; 'Makes' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to create something is to bring it into being, to make it.

clue.text: Whistleblower stopped by English bank (4)

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a hole, so the letter blocks the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A leaker of secrets silenced by an English bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistleblower' wants to be an informant; here it is the referee on a football pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge or bank of rock or sand near the surface of the sea.

clue.text: Underground organisation, as in secret moving? (10)

indicators.note: letters that move change places

explanation.surface: Asking whether an underground movement travels in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: The wartime Resistance in occupied France worked in secret, so the fodder describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A resistance is an underground movement fighting an occupying power.

clue.text: Displays breakfast containers? (10)

blocks.note: to brandish is to wave about for show
bowls for a high-fibre cereal made from husks

explanation.surface: A kitchen shop showing off its cereal bowls.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BRAN DISHES for the second meaning; the question mark flags that split.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandishes means waves or displays something ostentatiously.

clue.text: Replace wonderful children after daughter moves west (9)

indicators.note: in an across answer west is left, so the D shifts one place towards the front

blocks.note: SEED = children (offspring); its D moves left, giving SEDE

explanation.surface: Swapping in marvellous new children after a daughter emigrates west.
explanation.walkthrough: The daughter is not added: D is already in SEED and only slides one place left.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a new model supersedes the old one by taking its place.

clue.text: Remarkably different bird, catching insect finally (9)

indicators.note: the bird catches the letter and holds it

explanation.surface: An unusual bird snapping up an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes into STARLING after the fourth letter; the bird catching an insect is also the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Startling means so unusual as to be surprising.

clue.text: Mean to shun male bore (5)

indicators.note: to shun is to avoid, so the male letter is left out

explanation.surface: A stingy man avoiding a tedious fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean to' wants to be 'intend to' and 'bore' a dull person; the bore is a tidal wave running up a river, and EAGRE is its old name.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagre is a tidal bore, a wave surging up an estuary.

clue.text: Dog wrecked tea garden (5,4)

indicators.note: something wrecked is broken up

explanation.surface: A dog ruining a garden cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a dog rampaging through a tea garden, and this breed is big enough to do real damage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is a very large breed of dog.

clue.text: Article containing argument for protective cover (5)

indicators.note: the article holds the other piece inside

blocks.note: a pro is an argument in favour, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece arguing the case for protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' does double work in the surface; 'argument for' is PRO, and the final 'for' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is worn to protect clothes.

clue.text: Despatched to restrict a crowd in religious ceremony (9)

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the outer word closes round the rest

blocks.note: to cram is to crowd in

explanation.surface: Officers sent to hold back a crowd at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crowd' looks like a noun; here it is the verb, to CRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrament is a religious rite such as baptism or communion.

clue.text: Sleep in small cabin with study (4-3)

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
to eye is to study closely

explanation.surface: Nodding off in a tiny cabin that has a study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' only links; the pieces sit side by side, not one inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom: getting some shut-eye means closing your eyes to sleep.

clue.text: Go up, moving out in line (6)

indicators.note: the letters named move out of the word

blocks.note: to increase is to go up
these letters move out of INCREASE

explanation.surface: Rising and moving out while standing in a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In line' reads as queuing; 'in' is the part to remove and 'line' alone is the definition, the crease on a cricket pitch or a fold.
explanation.definitionFit: A crease is a line, whether a fold in cloth or a marked line in cricket.

clue.text: Word currently employed succeeded “limits” (10)

explanation.surface: A remark that the word 'limits' is now in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'limits' look like the word being discussed; it is just the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a terminus is an end point, the limit of a line or route.

clue.text: Lots of paper getting left in field (5)

indicators.note: the paper gets, or receives, the letter
the letter goes in the paper word

explanation.surface: Heaps of paper abandoned in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like 'abandoned' and 'field' like a meadow; they are L and a sphere of activity.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sphere of knowledge can be called a field or a realm.

clue.text: Restless desire barely fits companion (4)

indicators.note: bared of its outer letters, like something stripped

blocks.note: FITS with its outside letters stripped

explanation.surface: A restless urge that only just suits a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely fits' reads as 'only just fits'; it strips F and S from FITS.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative use: an itch for travel is a nagging craving, like a skin irritation that will not settle.

clue.text: Woman receiving honour for successful hit in US (5)

indicators.note: the woman receives the honour inside her

explanation.surface: An American woman honoured for a big success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' is American slang for a home run in baseball, a hit that lets the batter round every base.
explanation.definitionFit: A homer is a home run, the best possible hit in baseball.

clue.text: Slimmed down after reducing starchy food (4)

indicators.note: the phrase is cut down to a short piece of itself

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words: the last two of one and the first two of the other

explanation.surface: Someone slimmer after cutting out starchy food.
explanation.walkthrough: The diet surface is the disguise: 'Slimmed down' holds the answer, and an eddo is taro, a starchy root.
explanation.definitionFit: The eddo is the taro root, a starchy tuber eaten in the tropics.

clue.text: Millions stolen from Russian ruler in novel (7)

indicators.note: what is stolen is taken away

blocks.note: M = millions, the letter taken out
in = at HOME; the M is stolen from it

explanation.surface: Millions looted from a tsar, told in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is HOME, as in 'staying in'; the M comes out of that, not out of the ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivanhoe is Walter Scott's novel of medieval England.

clue.text: Model admires piece to be worn (7)

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A fashion model admiring an item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' is slang for a gun, so a piece to be worn is a holstered weapon, not a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang meets straight sense: 'piece' is gangster slang for a gun, and this is the gun carried on the hip.

clue.text: Better rest up after match (8)

indicators.note: stirred up, so the letters are mixed
this piece comes after the other

explanation.surface: Advice to rest after a match to feel better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as 'improved'; it is one who bets, and a gamester is a gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamester is a gambler, someone who bets.

clue.text: Show-off regrets work being sent back (6)

indicators.note: sent back, so the letters run the other way

explanation.surface: A show-off regretting having their work rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: Opus is the usual crossword 'work', shortened; the whole string turns round, not each piece separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A poseur is someone who poses to impress, a show-off.
